chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Pops Foster's string bass changes New York bands
summary: Only Ellington used string bass, with Wellman Braud, until Pops Foster's style spread; guitars were the last instrument bands hired.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, with Pops Foster on the string bass, that was somewhat unusual, because weren't most of the bands still playing tubas?
They were playing tubas. In fact, the only
band at that time that was using a string bass was Duke Ellington.
Well, Foster was also from New Orleans. So the New Orleans basses were usually string.

Well, when they had a bass, it was a string bass. In fact, Pops Foster changed the style in New York. See, they didn't change... See, Braud had been playing here for years, string bass, with Duke, and even before Duke. He didn't need nothin'. Soon as Pops Foster come around with the bass, then they all started to change it around, playing his style(?) on the bass.
Would you say at about the same time the banjo was fading out in favor of the guitar, or...?

No, it was before that. The guitar... It was all right; the banjo was all right in the band. Well, I guess... Well, I would say around the same time. But neither one of them was too popular in bands. They were being used in some bands, and some bands they weren't. But guitar had a hard way to go. They were usually the last ones to be hired in a band. They would even come behind the trombones; they would hire the trombones before they could have a guitar!
Well, it was hard for a guitar to be heard.
It would, yeah. But then they come into their day... They're in their day now. They're havin' their day now. They really got it now.
